blocks.text: Pihahiroth, Migdol, and Baal-zephon present an ordered route and camping setting around the sea. These names are part of the narrative's geographic evidence, but matching each one to a modern location remains disputed. Keeping that distinction in view prevents any familiar modern map from being treated as the only route permitted by the passage.

The sea crossing is a decisive act of deliverance, but it is not the endpoint of Exodus. The book continues from deliverance to covenant, then to covenant breach and renewal, the construction of the tabernacle, and the arrival of divine glory. Reading these as connected movements shows that release from Egypt leads into the formation of Israel's covenant life and the account of God's presence among the people.
